subject: FinEx - Post-call: performance & throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Garcia <tom.garcia@finexpayments.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finexpayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: FinEx - Post-call: performance & throughput follow-up

Hi Tom / Priya — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use case: fraud alert enrichment and conversational assistant in the payments UI. Mix of short, latency-sensitive queries and longer contextual generations for dispute summaries.
- Latency target: p95 <= 300ms for short queries, p95 <= 800ms acceptable for summary generation.
- Throughput: baseline ~150 qps steady-state, peak bursts up to 700 qps for flash sale windows.
- Concurrency: expected 400 concurrent active user sessions during peak windows; average session issues 3 requests/sec when active.
- Streaming: streaming partial responses for the assistant is required for product feel on mobile/web.

Open clarifying questions:
1) For the "short queries" category, can you confirm median and p95 token lengths (prompt + expected response)?
2) Do you have a hard SLA we should price against (e.g., formal p95 latency target tied to credits)?
3) Any data residency or private deployment constraints beyond US region?

Attached: finex_mvp_requirements.xlsx (your inputs from the discovery form) and a quick Redwood throughput model (redwood_throughput_model_v1.pdf) — the latter shows a starting estimate for GPUs required for different token-per-second and concurrency combinations.

Next steps:
- If you can share sample traffic patterns (per-hour QPS for a typical week) and token-length distributions, we’ll run a sizing model and come back with recommended configs and a cost range.
- Propose a 60-min deep dive next week (Marissa + Neha + Rafael) to go through streaming implementation and fallback behaviors.

Thanks — Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finexpayments.com>

Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:26:00 -0500
Subject: Re: FinEx - Post-call: performance & throughput follow-up

Thanks Rafael — quick answers inline.

> Latency target: p95 <= 300ms for short queries
We are aiming for p95 <= 200ms for the truly short reads (card-status checks, risk flags). For richer conversational responses p95 <= 600-800ms is fine.

> Baseline ~150 qps steady-state, peak bursts up to 700 qps
Baseline is accurate for daytime volume. Peak 700 qps is a good working number — during big marketing promos we have seen sustained 10-15 minute peaks.

> Concurrency: expected 400 concurrent active user sessions
This is roughly right; our backend opens a socket per active session and many sessions stay idle for minutes.

Token lengths (rough median / p95): short queries median ~25 tokens, p95 ~75 tokens; summaries median ~350 tokens, p95 ~900 tokens.

Streaming: yes, we need chunked responses for the assistant. Ideally client displays token-by-token or small-chunk updates.

On SLA / credits: we do not have a formal credits/rebates SLA in the initial POC, but we care about predictable p95 performance.

I’ll upload a day-of-week QPS CSV from our analytics team by EOD Monday.

-Priya

Priya — perfect, thanks for the token and latency details, that helps a lot. A few follow-ups so we can size accurately: 

1) For streaming: can you confirm whether clients keep the same connection open across multiple requests (session affinity) or open new connections per request? This affects connection overhead and selection of RPC vs long-poll streaming.
2) For the 700 qps peak: is that measured as requests/sec or inference requests/sec (i.e., do you batch multiple logical user actions into a single inference call)?
3) Any constraints on response truncation vs asynchronous background generation (e.g., do you prefer a short immediate response and background longer summary delivered by webhook)?

I've attached a small sizing worksheet (finex_mvp_requirements.xlsx) populated with your numbers and a Redwood rough model. From a first-pass estimate using your p95 sizes and streaming needs, ballpark GPU requirements for steady-state 150 qps (mixed short + summaries) vs 700 qps peak: 
- Steady-state (150 qps): ~4 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs with continuous batching and prefix cache.
- Peak (700 qps sustained for 10-15 minutes): need burst capacity or autoscale to ~18 A100-equivalent GPUs unless you accept degraded p95.
- Connection handling & streaming: recommend an edge routing pattern with sticky sessions to keep streaming latency down and avoid cold KV cache misses.

Propose we run these numbers against a Redwood dedicated cluster config in a quick model — Marissa / Neha, can you take point on running the sizing with the uploaded CSV once Priya sends it?

If this looks right, I'll propose two time options for the deep-dive: Wed Nov 24 @ 10am PT or Thu Nov 25 @ 9am PT.

Thanks — Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FinEx - Post-call: performance & throughput follow-up

Thanks Priya, Rafael — and thanks for the CSV in advance. Quick note from the infra/opt side before the deep-dive: 

- We’ll model two traffic profiles: (A) steady-state 150 qps with median tokens, (B) sustained 700 qps peak with p95 token sizes. For (B) we’ll run both an autoscale plan and a burst-capacity plan using pre-warmed instances to avoid cold-cache penalties.
- For streaming, our recommended approach is HTTP/2 server-sent chunks with sticky routing to preserve KV cache. That gives close-to-token streaming behavior with lower connection overhead than websockets for your topology.
- Initial quantization: we’ll test int8 profiles for summary generation to reduce GPU memory and increase effective throughput; we’ll measure latency delta on summary workload and feed it back before the call.

Action items for the deep-dive (Marissa + Neha + Rafael):
1) Review the uploaded CSV and confirm hour-by-hour QPS distribution.
2) Walk through the streaming implementation details (sticky sessions, chunking) and any client constraints.
3) Review a costed configuration (dedicated vs hosted burst) and show expected p95 and cost per 1M requests.

Priya/Tom — can you confirm Wed Nov 24 @ 10am PT or Thu Nov 25 @ 9am PT? We’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda.

Cheers — Marissa

--
